items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: the band was a home town band called Monk Mollencup and His Society Orchestra

ctx.x: But, at that early age though, you could pick up songs just by hearing them once or twice, couldn't you?

Oh, yes. I always had a good ear for memorizing the lead to a song. The melody as it were. And, so, uh, all I did was strive to improve and I remember once -- this is running ahead of myself here, but-- once, being with a band and the piano player was very good; the band was a home town band called Monk Mollencup and His Society Orchestra and, occasionally, he'd have me and his band play the banjo. So, the piano player leaned over to me one night and said - "Why the hell don't you learn how to play the banjo?"…

the right chord and he actually taught me how to play the banjo because he couldn't stand the way I played it. And, uh, it wasn't-- there wasn't any doubt that I was the worst one in the band, but I was determined to learn -- I really was. And, so, I used to play several jobs with him, but he mapped that thing out to me and I went home with that - that thing he wrote for me, you know, and I studied it. I really did, you know and I got to the point where I could read, as you know, all the music for a piano - had…
